items.topic: Where to publish the contract document
items.context: Actions currently name `docs/deployment/desktop-runtime-discovery-contract.md`. Confirm this is the right home. The initiative is about desktop runtime interop, which fits under deployment docs; alternative is an internal architecture location under `docs/internal/` which is less discoverable but reads more as a spec than a deployment guide.

options.label: `docs/deployment/desktop-runtime-discovery-contract.md`, linked from `docs/deployment/README.md`
options.rationale: Deployment docs are where readers look for desktop / packaging behavior, and the Deployment Hub is already the referenced jumping-off point in CLAUDE.md. Best discoverability for the people who will implement and operate this.

options.label: `docs/internal/desktop-runtime-discovery-contract.md`, linked from an internal index
options.rationale: Treats the contract as a normative internal spec and keeps it alongside other SEAMS-style docs. Lower discoverability for integrators; better signal that this is a stable engineering contract.

options.label: Both — short deployment-doc explainer that links to an authoritative internal spec
options.rationale: Maximum coverage but duplicates the authoritative statement in two places and risks drift.

items.topic: Scope of the regression matrix for handoff
items.context: The Regression Matrix section lists 10 cases. Cases 1–7 are core semantics, 8–9 are Windows parity, 10 is a concurrent-start stress case. Swarm Manager's guidance is to favor automated regression tests; `execute/desktop-ecosystem-interop-regression-coverage` already owns implementation. The question is which cases are mandatory for 'contract proven' versus nice-to-have.

options.label: Mandatory: 1–9. Case 10 (concurrent start) is nice-to-have, noted as a future hardening.
options.rationale: Covers the full semantic and cross-platform contract without forcing the regression suite to build a race-condition harness on day one. Concurrent-start races are a robustness property, not a contract property.

options.label: Mandatory: 1–10. All cases treated as launch-gating.
options.rationale: Most defensive and complete. Also the slowest and most brittle test suite, and case 10 may not be reliably reproducible without a specialized harness.

options.label: Mandatory: 1–6 (semantic core). 7–10 are follow-ups.
options.rationale: Smallest launch gate. But makes Windows parity and the override seam optional at launch, which contradicts the initiative goals.

items.topic: Treatment of legacy records with empty `source`
items.context: The contract specifies that records with `source == ""` (legacy swarm-written records with no Source field) are treated as `source = "swarm"` for precedence purposes. This is the natural backward-compat choice, but worth an explicit call so the `execute/cross-platform-bundled-discovery-parity` implementer does not have to rediscover it.

options.label: Empty `source` → treat as `"swarm"` for precedence. Document in the contract.
options.rationale: Preserves behavior: all existing records today have no source and belong to the swarm. Precedence logic stays `bundle > swarm|empty`, which is the expected invariant. Zero migration required.

options.label: Backfill: swarm lifecycle starts writing `source: "swarm"` explicitly as part of this change; empty `source` becomes an error.
options.rationale: Cleanest going forward, but requires coordinated deploy of swarm lifecycle and bundle lifecycle and creates a window where older swarm CLIs write records that newer resolvers reject. Overkill.

items.text: Verified in round 3: `internal/process/process.go::LiveRecords()` (lines 146-161) already iterates every record through `isPIDRunningFn(record.PID)` and drops records with dead PIDs. `Port()` resolution already feeds records through this filter, so stale-bundle-record handling (D3=A from round 2) is not a new primitive — it's the mechanism the CLI already uses for dead swarm records. This reduces the implementation surface of `execute/cross-platform-bundled-discovery-parity` by one item.

Verified in round 3: adding `Source string \`json:"source,omitempty\"\`` to `process.Record` is cleanly backward-compatible. Legacy records unmarshal with Source="" (no error), older readers ignore the field entirely, and `omitempty` keeps JSON narrow when the field is unset. The swarm lifecycle does not have to change — it can keep writing records without Source and the resolver will treat them as swarm records.

Survey finding: no existing code under `scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/runtime/` references `~/.vrooli/processes/` or `process.WriteScenarioRecord`. The bundle registration integration is greenfield inside the bundle runtime, so the implementer of `execute/cross-platform-bundled-discovery-parity` can choose the cleanest call site (likely adjacent to `service_launcher.go` where a service successfully comes up and the real port is known) without untangling existing coupling.

Precedence enforcement is estimated as ~10 lines in `internal/app/scenario/service.go::Port()`: after `BuildListPorts` returns candidate live records, if any candidate has `Source=="bundle"`, keep only those; else keep the set as-is. No api-core change, no resolver change, no new file. This keeps the desktop-first invariant isolated to the CLI and makes it trivially unit-testable with synthetic record fixtures.

This research item appears ready for conclusion after this round: problem clarity, scope, methodology, and risk awareness are all at 3; testable is at 2 pending the regression-matrix scoping decision (D2). Once D1-D3 are answered the conclusion is actionable as-is and both sibling execute items have everything they need to proceed.

plan_updates: Conclusion rewritten for settled state: Summary now states the contract in one paragraph; added Findings 4-6 (LiveRecords already handles liveness; Source field is additive; ~10-line precedence patch) and Finding 8 (greenfield bundle registration call site); added a dedicated 'Contract Summary (Final Form)' section with default precedence, resolution semantics, bundle participation, schema change, cross-platform table, and override seam; added a 'Regression Matrix' section with 10 numbered cases categorized as core semantic (1-7), Windows parity (8-9), and stress (10); populated Actions with doc-publish targets and explicit hand-off guidance (no new backlog items); tightened Limitations to just the real residual unknowns (tiebreakers, PID reuse, multi-install, XDG migration, no network layer).
